summary.text: Democrat Hannah Pingree won the election for governor of Maine on November 3, 2026, defeating Bobby Charles, according to unofficial results, and is set to take office when the new term begins.

She served in the Maine House of Representatives from 2002 to 2010, including as Speaker from 2008 to 2010, and directed Gov. Janet Mills's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future from 2019 to 2025.

paragraphs.text: Pingree was born in Belfast, Maine, grew up on North Haven, and graduated from Brown University in 1998 with a degree in political science.

She served four terms in the Maine House of Representatives from 2002 to 2010, representing District 36, chairing the Health and Human Services Committee, serving as Majority Leader from 2006 to 2008 and as Speaker from 2008 to 2010.
From 2019 to 2025 Pingree directed the Governor's Office of Policy Innovation and the Future under Gov. Janet Mills.
She won the November 3, 2026 general election for Governor of Maine with 54.5% of the vote to Bobby Charles's 37.4% and Rick Bennett's 8.1%, according to unofficial results reported by NBC News.
